I have farmed these 7 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I never went to school, so I don’t read those extension papers — I learn by watching my neighbors and remembering what happened on my own fields. My household has six people, and some of my family work in the city and send money home, which helps with cash, but it also means I have fewer hands at home during busy times. I must count every yuan I spend on inputs.

My wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I planted about 5 mu of improved wheat — the same seed everyone in the village uses, something like Jimai or Luyuan. Before sowing last fall, I rotary-tilled the land. Now that spring is here, I will topdress with urea twice: once at green-up and again at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. I also put down compound fertilizer at planting, so altogether that is about 16 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times from my well — at green-up, at heading, and once more in late May if the weather turns dry. Pumping costs electricity, but I cannot let the wheat dry out. I will spray herbicide once and fungicide two or three times because the leaf rust comes every year no matter what.

After wheat harvest in early June, I have only a few days before I must plant summer maize on that same 5 mu. There is no time to plough, so I hire my neighbor’s no-tillage seeder. I plant hybrid maize seed — usually Denghai or whatever good hybrid the seed shop has — because the big ears pay back the seed cost. I put compound fertilizer in the holes at planting and sidedress urea when the maize is knee-high, about 14 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice if the rains don’t come, and spray for weeds and corn borers. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

I keep 2 mu for peanut because my family likes the oil and the market price is decent. Peanut needs loose soil, so I rotary-till that plot well in spring. I use improved peanut seed. I don’t put much nitrogen because the plant makes its own, but I add phosphorus and potassium so the pods fill out — about 5 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice and spray for leaf spot and aphids. I hope for about 280 kg per mu of pods.
